items.title: Siemens: an AI agent platform for the US workforce
items.role: AI Product Strategist, XPS Program
items.summary: Built and launched Spark AI, a 120+ agent platform for 1,000+ Siemens US employees across every major function, and presented a 3/6/12-month AI roadmap to US leadership.
items.confidentiality_note: Details are under NDA; this describes my role and approach, not proprietary specifics.
items.body_md:
## Context
In summer 2026 I worked at Siemens as an AI Product Strategist in the XPS Program, focused on the Siemens US organization. The assignment was enterprise AI adoption: getting AI into the daily work of employees across every major function, not only engineering.

## The problem
At the start of the summer, few people across the US organization used AI in their daily work. The work was to give employees in each function, at each level of seniority, AI tools built for their own jobs, get them to actually use those tools, and leave leadership with a plan for the next 12 months.

## My role
My manager originated the idea for the platform. I built and launched it, drove adoption across the organization, and wrote and presented the roadmap for what should come next.

## What I built / did
- Built and launched Spark AI, a custom AI platform for Siemens US made up of 120+ custom agents and 50+ custom skills, built for specific job functions and seniority levels rather than as one general assistant.
- Deployed it across 1,000+ employees spanning all major job functions.
- Designed and presented a 3/6/12-month AI transformation roadmap to Siemens US leadership. It was sequenced by each function's readiness, mapped the dependencies between steps, and tied role-specific success metrics to measurable workflow efficiency outcomes.

## How I worked
I wrote a product spec first and built against checklists with acceptance criteria. At the end of the summer I demoed the platform live to the team and walked through what worked and what did not.

## What I'd do differently
More QA before each release, and a steadier cadence of smaller releases instead of large drops.

items.title: National Grid: a cloud and AI platform for a siloed enterprise
items.role: Principal Product Manager
items.summary: Owned the cloud and AI/ML roadmap at a 20,000-person utility: launched a RAG-based generative AI platform to 3,000+ monthly users and grew digital services revenue from $2M to $20M+ annualized.
items.confidentiality_note: Details are under NDA; this describes my role and approach, not proprietary specifics.
items.body_md:
## Context
National Grid is a 20,000-person Fortune 500 utility. From 2022 to 2025 I was a product manager there, promoted from Technical to Senior to Principal Product Manager. I owned the strategic cloud and AI/ML roadmap.

## The problem
Engineering was organized in silos. Each business unit ran its own infrastructure, and adopting a tool meant a separate procurement and security review for every team. Deploying a cloud service took weeks. Engineers and support teams also needed faster answers from internal documentation. Product management was new to much of the organization; the data science team saw it as overhead.

## My role
Principal Product Manager. I set the cloud and AI/ML roadmap, prototyped AI systems alongside engineers, explained technical strategy and business value to the C-suite, and turned the strategy into engineering plans. I grew the team from 1 to 4 pods and hired and developed 4 product managers.

## What I built / did
- Designed and launched an internal generative AI platform that connected an LLM (GPT) to proprietary documentation through retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), so engineers and support teams resolved issues faster.
- Built an Infrastructure as Code (IaC) service and standardized 100+ enterprise tools (AKS, Snowflake, Power BI) across all business units, with no separate procurement or security review per team.
- Founded Cloud Leadership Sync, the company's first executive and Chief Architect-level cross-business-unit forum, and introduced portfolio-level roadmapping, PRDs and agile ceremonies across all business units.
- Ran individual stakeholder campaigns to get every business unit President and Chief Architect to give up infrastructure autonomy. Presidents heard about removing an engineering tax; Chief Architects heard about production-grade tooling without a security review burden.

## Results
- Digital services revenue grew from $2M to $20M+ annualized.
- The generative AI platform reached 3,000+ monthly active users.
- Cloud service deployment went from weeks to minutes.
- The engineering organization grew from 5 to 35 engineers.
- 2 of the 4 product managers I hired were promoted to senior within 12 months.

## How I worked
Most of the job was persuasion without authority. I pitched each audience on its own problem rather than giving one deck to everyone. I won over the data science team through embedded discovery and their own data, until their view moved from "product management is overhead" to "product management is why our models get used." The documents were the standard product set, applied at portfolio scale: PRDs, portfolio roadmaps, a recurring executive forum, and engineering plans translated from strategy.

items.title: Deloitte: machine learning for Fortune 100 clients
items.role: Machine Learning Consultant
items.summary: ML and data work on Fortune 100 engagements: an ML contact-center product for Pfizer that cut average queue time from 75 to 15 minutes, and a clustering model for GM that saved $17.5M.
items.confidentiality_note: Details are under NDA; this describes my role and approach, not proprietary specifics.
items.body_md:
## Context
From 2020 to 2022 I was a Machine Learning Consultant at Deloitte, working on engagements for Fortune 100 clients including Pfizer, General Motors and Walmart. At the same time I took graduate coursework in data science through Georgia Tech's OMSA program. I was promoted to senior in my first year, in the top 5% of my new-hire class.

## The problem
Each engagement was a different problem. During COVID-19, a contact center was overwhelmed and wait times were long. A manufacturer was carrying configurations that cost more than they returned. A retailer needed its data moved onto a new platform without losing the ability to run analytics at scale.

## My role
I worked on the machine learning and data side of consulting engagements, including hands-on ML engineering: managing the development of ML products, designing and deploying models, and designing data architecture. I also synthesized market research, competitive analysis and operational data into recommendations clients could act on.

## What I built / did
- Pfizer: managed the development of an ML-integrated contact-center product during COVID-19 that automated response generation for incoming requests.
- General Motors: designed and deployed a clustering algorithm (unsupervised machine learning) to identify and prune low-value configurations.
- Walmart: led a data migration to SAP S/4HANA and designed the data architecture for scalable analytics operations.

## Results
- Pfizer: average queue time fell from 75 minutes to 15.
- General Motors: the configuration pruning saved $17.5M.
- Promoted to senior in year one, top 5% of the new-hire class.

items.title: Brio Energy: sales and accounting systems for a solar company
items.role: Senior Full-Stack Developer / Product Owner
items.summary: Built a custom CRM that cut the sales-to-accounting turnaround from 5 days to 15 minutes, a marketing site producing 175+ qualified leads a week, and microservices that cut accounting spend by $745K a year.
items.confidentiality_note: Details are under NDA; this describes my role and approach, not proprietary specifics.
items.body_md:
## Context
From 2018 to 2020 I was a Senior Full-Stack Developer and Product Owner at Brio Energy, a solar company. I wrote the code and also decided what to build.

## The problem
The sales and accounting teams worked out of systems that did not fit how the business ran. Handing work from sales to accounting took about five days. The company needed a steadier flow of qualified leads, and accounting costs were higher than they needed to be.

## My role
I was both a builder and the product owner. I scoped the problems with the sales and accounting teams, decided what to build first, and built it.

## What I built / did
- Built a custom CRM for the solar sales division from scratch, designed around the hand-off between sales and accounting.
- Launched a new marketing website built to generate qualified leads for the sales organization.
- Designed and deployed backend microservices that reduced what the accounting department spent.

## Results
- The sales-to-accounting turnaround went from 5 days to 15 minutes.
- The marketing website generated 175+ qualified leads per week, contributing to $3.9M in annual new revenue across the sales organization.
- The microservices reduced accounting department spend by $745K annually, measured against the prior-year run rate.
